scalars.scalar_value: Bachelor’s degree or equivalent is required.

A minimum of ten years of progressively responsible leadership experience in alumni relations, constituent engagement, advancement, events management, higher education administration, nonprofit leadership, or a related field is required.

items.item_text: A valid driver’s license is required or equivalent means of reliable transportation to off-site meetings and events.
Bachelor’s degree or equivalent is required. Master’s degree is preferred.

A minimum of ten years of progressively responsible leadership experience in alumni relations, constituent engagement, advancement, events management, higher education administration, nonprofit leadership, or a related field is required.
In partnership with the CEEO, develop and implement a multi-year engagement and experience strategy aligned with institutional priorities, campaign goals, and Advancement objectives.
Serve as a leader within Advancement and the Experience and Engagement team, helping shape the College’s constituent engagement vision.
Advance innovative, constituent-centered engagement and experience programs that strengthen lifelong relationships and institutional affinity.
Establish goals, performance measures, and assessment frameworks to evaluate participation, experience quality, volunteer engagement, and overall impact.
Monitor emerging trends and best practices in engagement, volunteer leadership, constituent experience, and events management.
Design engagement pathways that move constituents from connection to participation, volunteer leadership, and philanthropy.
Establish standards for hospitality, accessibility, inclusion, and service excellence across engagement programs and events.

Lead a culture of assessment and continuous improvement through the strategic use of data, constituent feedback, CASE Alumni Engagement Metrics, and performance reporting to measure impact, inform decision-making, and advance institutional goals.

Build, lead, and develop a high-performing engagement and events team by establishing clear priorities, promoting professional growth, and fostering a culture of collaboration, innovation, accountability, and service.
Provide strategic oversight of departmental budgets, staffing, resource allocation, and operational planning to ensure organizational effectiveness and achievement of institutional goals.
Work collaboratively with the Advancement Communications Team to support the strategy and development of print and digital communications that support programming and strategic objectives.
Provide strategic oversight of the College’s alumni, family, volunteer, and student-to-alumni engagement programs and initiatives.

Develop and execute integrated engagement strategies that increase participation, strengthen affinity and belonging, expand volunteer leadership, and support lifelong engagement and philanthropic readiness.

Serve as advisor, chief budget officer, and Treasurer of the Alumni Association Board and other volunteer leadership groups, ensuring their work advances institutional priorities and campaign objectives.
Oversee reunions, affinity programs, regional engagement, mentoring, networking opportunities, lifelong learning initiatives, volunteer programs, and other signature engagement experiences.

Develop and strengthen volunteer pathways that support mentoring, career engagement, admissions, campaign participation, ambassadorship, and philanthropy, while building sustainable leadership pipelines and succession plans.
Partner with colleagues across Advancement and the College to create seamless pathways from student engagement to alumni engagement and strengthen lifelong connections to Pomona.
Expand meaningful family engagement opportunities and alumni-student connections through networking, mentoring, professional development, and experiential learning opportunities.
Ensure care and stewardship of the College’s Seaver Alumni House facilities.

Provide strategic leadership and oversight of the Office of College Events and the College’s comprehensive events portfolio, ensuring alignment with institutional priorities, academic objectives, and the Pomona College mission.

Lead the development of a campus-wide events and experience strategy that advances the College’s educational mission, strengthens community, elevates constituent experiences, and enhances Pomona’s reputation among internal and external audiences.

Leverage the College’s events portfolio as a strategic platform for advancing Pomona’s academic mission, strengthening community, building institutional affinity, enhancing visibility and reputation, and creating meaningful connections among students, families, alumni, faculty, staff, community members, and external partners.

Partner with academic and administrative departments, faculty, senior leaders, and campus stakeholders to design meaningful experiences and support programs, conferences, lectures, ceremonies, traditions, and special events that enrich the intellectual, cultural, and community life of the College.

Oversee the successful execution of major institutional events, including Commencement, Family Weekend, Alumni Weekend, Founders Day, presidential and trustee events, campaign events, donor experiences, academic conferences, and other signature programs.

Establish and maintain standards for hospitality, accessibility, inclusion, service excellence, budget stewardship, and operational effectiveness that ensure a consistent and exceptional Pomona experience across all events and programs.

Foster a culture of collaboration, innovation, assessment, and continuous improvement, utilizing feedback and performance measures to strengthen event effectiveness, audience experience, and institutional impact.

Provide strategic oversight of conference services, facility rentals, filming opportunities, and external partnerships that generate revenue while supporting the College’s mission, priorities, and stewardship of campus resources.

In partnership with the Director of the Office of College Events and campus stakeholders, develop and execute growth strategies that expand earned revenue through conferences, rentals, filming opportunities, and external partnerships while preserving the integrity of the academic environment and campus experience.

Ensure achievement of annual earned-revenue goals and identify opportunities to strengthen community visibility, institutional partnerships, and the College’s reputation through thoughtfully aligned external engagements.
Evaluate and pursue strategic opportunities that balance revenue generation, mission alignment, constituent experience, and long-term institutional value.
Partner with Advancement leadership to develop engagement strategies that support campaign goals and institutional priorities.
Create experiences and participation opportunities that increase campaign visibility, volunteer leadership, donor engagement, and community involvement.
Collaborate across Development, Annual Giving, Reunion Giving, Stewardship, and Advancement Communications to strengthen the engagement-to-philanthropy pipeline.
Represent the College at institutional, professional, and community events.
Participate in committees, initiatives, and special projects as assigned.
Perform other duties in support of the mission and strategic goals of the College.
